newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb destroys office building in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Bomb destroys office building in Corsica.

text.p: An overnight bomb in the southern Corsican port town of Propriano destroyed a building housing the local Chamber of Commerce, police said on Wednesday.

There were no injuries and no one immediately claimed responsibility, but police said it appeared to be the work of separatists who have waged a persistent but low-level guerrilla campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France for the past two decades.

Despite a threatened crackdown on lawlessness on the Mediterranean resort island, bombs have exploded regularly since mid-August, when one of the main nationalist groups called off a shaky truce intended to foster secret talks with the government.
The most recent bombing went undetected for hours because a violent rainstorm apparently covered up the sound of the blast.
The same building had previously been bombed and also sprayed by machine-gun fire in the past two years, police said.
"The damage is considerable. The entire building will have to be razed," a Chamber of Commerce spokesman said.
